author: EmuCore - Hub
title: Test Bluetooth audio without hiding controller latency
summary: Use the phone picture as the input reference, compare local and Bluetooth sound routes, and record controller-to-visual delay separately from visual-to-audio delay.
heroAlt: Shadow of Rome scene with a sharp visual action used to separate controller response from Bluetooth audio arrival

blocks.text: Time the picture before listening to the sound
Measure wireless sound delay separately from controller input delay so a late sound is not mistaken for a late button response.
Judging a control only by the sound it triggers combines input, rendering, and Bluetooth buffering into one misleading delay.
Prepare separate visual and audio markers

items: Immediate on-screen action with a distinct matching sound selected.
Controller connection kept unchanged across audio routes.
Phone display processing and refresh mode fixed.
1. Repeat the action through phone speakers and observe press-to-picture response.
2. Record picture-to-sound relationship for the local route.
3. Connect Bluetooth audio without reconnecting or remapping the controller.
4. Repeat the same action and scene several times.
5. Compare press-to-picture timing first, ignoring sound.
6. Then compare picture-to-sound timing between routes.
7. Move Bluetooth and Wi-Fi interference away for a dropout check.
8. Save route-specific notes without applying a controller timing workaround.

blocks.text: The phone screen timestamps input response, while changing only audio output reveals delay contributed after the game has already produced the frame.
Accept separate input and audio conclusions
Visual controller response remains stable while the documented Bluetooth route adds only its measured audio delay and no dropouts.

items: Controller-to-picture response is compared independently from sound.
Only the audio output route changes between paired runs.
Bluetooth delay and dropouts are documented for the exact device and codec path.
Picture reacts promptly but sound is late: the controller is not the source.
Picture and sound both slow in one scene: check emulation speed.
Wired audio is also late: investigate app or display synchronization.
Bluetooth produces bursts: repeat after reducing radio contention.

blocks.text: Return to local or wired audio
Disconnect the Bluetooth audio device and restore the local audio route plus its independent volume.
Codec, headset firmware, Android scheduling, and radio conditions can change latency; the result describes this route, not Bluetooth as a universal value.
